title: Menard Pressuremeter Modulus

V₀.description: Initial volume of probe at rest

Vm.description: Volume at midpoint of linear portion of curve

ΔP/ΔV.description: Slope of linear (pseudo-elastic) portion of pressure-volume curve

applicability: EM is NOT directly equivalent to Young's modulus E. For settlement calculations using Menard's method, EM is used with rheological factor α: E/EM = 1/α (α = 0.25–1.0 depending on soil type and EM/pL ratio). Design directly with Menard rules, or convert to E.

title: Menard Limit Pressure (Net)
applicability: Net limit pressure is the key parameter for Menard bearing capacity design: q_u = k × pL* + q₀ where k is a bearing capacity factor (function of foundation shape and depth).

title: Undrained Shear Strength from SBPMT (Cavity Expansion)
applicability: From Gibson & Anderson (1961) undrained cylindrical cavity expansion theory. Requires iteration (Su appears on both sides). Typical Ir = G/Su = 50–500 → ln(Ir) = 4–6. Applicable to SBPMT; less reliable for PBP due to disturbance.

title: Shear Modulus from Unload-Reload Loop

V.description: Current volume of cavity at start of unload

applicability: Gur from unload-reload loops is the best pressuremeter estimate of in-situ shear stiffness. Perform loop in the pseudo-elastic portion of the curve. Unload by ~50% of current net pressure. Gur ≈ G at small-to-medium strain (0.01–0.1%).

title: DMT Material Index
applicability: ID < 0.1: peat/organic. 0.1–0.6: clay. 0.6–1.8: silt. > 1.8: sand. Boundaries are approximate — silty soils may cross boundaries.

title: DMT Horizontal Stress Index

KD.description: Horizontal stress index (analogous to K₀ but amplified by penetration)

applicability: KD ≈ 2 for NC soils (OCR ≈ 1). KD increases with OCR. KD is the most useful single DMT parameter — correlates with OCR, K₀, Su, and liquefaction potential.

title: DMT Dilatometer Modulus
applicability: ED is NOT a Young's modulus — it is an intermediate parameter. Convert to constrained modulus M = RM × ED where RM depends on ID and KD. 34.7 is a theoretical factor from elastic solution for a loaded circular plate in a half-space.

title: OCR from DMT (Clays)
applicability: For clays (ID < 1.2). Reasonably reliable for OCR < 8–10. For highly OC clays, may overestimate. Site-specific calibration against oedometer results recommended.

title: Su from DMT (Clays)
applicability: For clays. Essentially combines SHANSEP framework (Su/σ'v = f(OCR)) with OCR from KD. Consistent with Su/σ'v0 = 0.22 for NC clay. Compare with vane and CPT Su values.

title: K₀ from DMT
applicability: Original Marchetti (1980) correlation for uncemented clays. Best for NC to lightly OC soils. For KD = 2 (NC): K₀ ≈ 0.47 (reasonable for NC clay with PI ~30). Less reliable for highly OC or cemented soils.
